inlines.v: WALLOW, verb intransitive [Latin , G. This verb seems to be connected with well, walk, etc.] 1. To roll ones body on the earth, in mire, or on other substance; to tumble and roll in water. Swine wallow in the mire. 2. To move heavily and clumsily. Part huge of bulk, wallowing unwieldy, enormous in their gait, tempest the ocean. [Unusual.] 3. To live in filth or gross vice; as man wallowing in his native impurity. WALLOW, verb transitive To roll ones body. WALLOW thyself in ashes. Jeremiah 6:26. WALLOW, noun A kind of rolling walk.
